sentences.text: Julia Scarlett Elizabeth Louis-Dreyfus -LRB- -LSB- ˈluːi_ˈdraɪfəs -RSB- born January 13 , 1961 -RRB- is an American actress , comedian , and producer .

She is known for her work in television comedy , including Saturday Night Live -LRB- 1982 -- 85 -RRB- , Seinfeld -LRB- 1989 -- 98 -RRB- , The New Adventures of Old Christine -LRB- 2006 -- 10 -RRB- , and Veep -LRB- 2012 -- present -RRB- .	Saturday Night Live	Saturday Night Live	Seinfeld	Seinfeld	The New Adventures of Old Christine	The New Adventures of Old Christine	Veep	Veep (TV series)
Louis-Dreyfus holds several records for most Primetime Emmy Award wins and nominations .	Primetime Emmy Award	Primetime Emmy Award

Louis-Dreyfus broke into comedy as a performer in The Practical Theatre Company in Chicago , Illinois , which led to her casting in the sketch show Saturday Night Live from 1982 to 1985 .	Saturday Night Live	Saturday Night Live	The Practical Theatre Company	The Practical Theatre Company

Her breakthrough came in 1990 with a nine-season run playing Elaine Benes on Seinfeld , one of the most critically and commercially successful sitcoms of all time .	Seinfeld	Seinfeld	Elaine Benes	Elaine Benes

Other notable television roles include Christine Campbell in The New Adventures of Old Christine , which had a five-season run on CBS , and her role as Selina Meyer in Veep , which has recently been renewed by HBO for a sixth season .	The New Adventures of Old Christine	The New Adventures of Old Christine	Veep	Veep (TV series)	Christine Campbell	Christine Campbell (character)	CBS	CBS	Selina Meyer	Selina Meyer	HBO	HBO

Louis-Dreyfus ' film roles have included Hannah and Her Sisters -LRB- 1986 -RRB- , National Lampoon 's Christmas Vacation -LRB- 1989 -RRB- , Deconstructing Harry -LRB- 1997 -RRB- , and Enough Said -LRB- 2013 -RRB- .	Hannah and Her Sisters	Hannah and Her Sisters	Deconstructing Harry	Deconstructing Harry	Enough Said	Enough Said (film)
She has voiced roles in several animated films , including A Bug 's Life -LRB- 1998 -RRB- and Planes -LRB- 2013 -RRB- .	Planes	Planes (film)
Louis-Dreyfus has received nine Emmy Awards , seven for acting and two for producing , with a total of 22 nominations throughout her career .	Emmy Awards	Emmy Awards

She has also received a Golden Globe Award , seven Screen Actors Guild Awards , five American Comedy Awards , and two Critics ' Choice Television Awards .	Golden Globe Award	Golden Globe Award	Screen Actors Guild Awards	Screen Actors Guild Awards	American Comedy Awards	American Comedy Awards

Louis-Dreyfus received a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame in 2010 , and was inducted into the Television Academy Hall of Fame in 2014 .	Hollywood Walk of Fame	Hollywood Walk of Fame	Television Academy Hall of Fame	Television Academy Hall of Fame
In 2016 , Time named Louis-Dreyfus one of the 100 most influential people in the world on the annual Time 100 list .	Time	Time (magazine)	Time 100	Time 100
